title: The normalized global scalar-completion comparison
statement: Let l be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_l with an embedding iota, and Y an arbitrary scheme. Use the completed integral coefficient sheaves and their fixed ordinary and completed scalar functors [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. There is a unique natural transformation from ordinary derived scalar extension to completed scalar extension whose component on every good (K-flat with flat terms) complex, followed by the completed representative comparison, equals the ordinary derived counit followed by the specified quotient-completion chain map. That chain map has the finite quotient tensor projections and zero shifted-product coordinate. On every derived-complete input [def-weil-derived-complete], this natural transformation is an isomorphism. The complete normalization equation is exactly scalarCompletion_existsUnique in the existing IntegralOperationsScalarComparisons module.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Lemma 6.8.2(1); normalized quotient-completion map in the first paragraph of blueprint lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition

proof.text: The two specified completed coefficient maps agree by their finite quotient projections. The already proved ordinaryScalarModelIso identifies their ordinary sheafified tensor functors; its termwise complex isomorphism induces an ordinary derived isomorphism e by the universal left-derived functor property. The derived component equation is e followed by the target counit equals the source counit followed by the localized ordinary complex comparison. Compose e with the existing completedScalarComparison. The latter normalization and integralScalarCompletionChain_model identify the resulting representative square with the exact required quotient-completion-chain square, including the zero shifted coordinate.

For an input satisfying IsSfDerivedComplete, choose a prime p greater than l and the auxiliary finite-field datum of characteristic p. The intrinsic/legacy completeness equivalence implies IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted for this same input. The finite-free completed scalar comparison proves that its specified completion component is invertible. The ordinary derived-model comparison e is a natural isomorphism, so its composite with that component is invertible as required. The auxiliary datum imposes no hypothesis on the scheme.

Good complexes localize to the ambient derived category. Two transformations with the stated normalization agree on the image of every good complex, by cancellation of its invertible completed representative comparison. Localization.natTrans_ext then proves equality on the whole derived category. This argument includes the zero complex, empty scheme, identity embedding, and arbitrary unbounded complete inputs.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedIntegralScalarCompletion (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L]
    (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L) (W : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃! χ : integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι W ⟶ integralScalarExtension l E L ι W,
      (∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory,
        χ.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫
            (integralScalarExtensionComparison l E L ι W).hom.app P =
          (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι W).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P.obj ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map ((integralScalarCompletionChain l E L ι W).app P.obj)) ∧
      (∀ K, IsSfDerivedComplete l E W K → IsIso (χ.app K))
lean.note: The full normalized completion proof is extracted to this module after explicit typed ordinary-counit and representative wrappers leave the complete item file over 60 seconds. The existing scalarCompletion_existsUnique declaration remains in IntegralOperationsScalarComparisons with its exact signature and is proved by applying this theorem after unfolding its normalization predicate. No statement or definition is weakened, and no new theorem hole is introduced.
